Codebook configuration guide

K.A. Stam & F. de Weijer

2026-11-13

Source: vignettes/codebook_configuration.Rmd
codebook_configuration.Rmd

Introduction

The YAML configuration is used to define the structure, types, and validation rules for each variable in the dataset.

Understanding the YAML structure

The YAML file consists of entries for each variable in your dataset. Each entry includes a description, units, type, categories, labels, and validation rules. Here is a breakdown of each component:

  • description: A brief explanation of the variable.
  • units: The units of measurement (if applicable).
  • type: The data type of the variable in R (e.g., character, numeric).
  • type_sql: The data type of the variable in SQL (e.g., VARCHAR(255), DECIMAL).
  • categories: A list of possible categories for categorical variables, separated by a semicolon without spaces (e.g., “M;F”).
  • labels: Labels for the categories, specifying the meaning of each category value. The format should use an equals sign (=) to associate each value with its label, without spaces around the equals sign. Each pair must be separated by a semicolon (;). Example: “0=No;1=Yes” or “M=Male;F=Female”.
  • validations: A list of validation rules to ensure data quality. The pointblank package is used for validation. Each validation rule is defined as a key-value pair where the key is the name of the validation function (e.g., col_is_character, col_vals_not_null, col_vals_regex, col_vals_between) and the value is a list of arguments for that function.
  • primary_key (optional): Set to true to mark this variable as the primary key of the table. Only one variable per codebook should carry this flag.
  • foreign_key (optional): A reference in the format <table>.<column> (e.g., study.study_id) that indicates this variable links to a column in another table.

Example YAML configuration

Here is an example of two variables in a YAML codebook — one primary key and one foreign key:

participant_id:
  description: ID given to the subject/volunteer of the study.
  primary_key: true
  units: ~
  type: character
  type_sql: VARCHAR(255)
  categories: ~
  labels: ~
  validations:
    - col_is_character: []
    - col_vals_not_null:
        label: "Participant ID is required"
    - rows_distinct:
        label: "Participant IDs are unique"

study_id:
  description: Identifier of the study this participant belongs to.
  foreign_key: study.study_id
  units: ~
  type: character
  type_sql: VARCHAR(255)
  categories: ~
  labels: ~
  validations:
    - col_is_character: []
    - col_vals_not_null:
        label: "Study ID is required"

Version semantics

Each codebook YAML has a top-level version field (e.g., 1.2).

  • Major version bump (e.g., 1.x → 2.x): drops and recreates the corresponding database table.
  • Minor version bump (e.g., 1.1 → 1.2): updates metadata only; existing data is preserved.

See Codebook Reference for the full list of available codebooks.

Adding custom codebooks

beFAIR’s built-in codebooks cover standard study, experiment, and analysis tables. For assays or schemas that are specific to your project, you can place custom YAML codebooks in the codebooks/ folder that startProject() creates inside every FAIRground directory.

Folder structure

Custom codebooks mirror the package layout:

MyProject/
├── codebooks/
│   ├── study/          ← study-level custom schemas
│   ├── experiment/     ← experiment-level custom schemas
│   └── analyses/       ← analysis-level custom schemas

Place your YAML file in the subdirectory that matches its pillar, e.g. codebooks/analysis/my_analysis.yaml.

Writing a custom codebook YAML

Custom codebooks use exactly the same format as the built-in ones. The minimum required fields at the top level are version, name, and variables. The primary_key and foreign_key fields on individual variables are optional:

version: 1.0
name: my_analysis
authors: Jane Doe
created_at: 2026-03-23
updated_at: 2026-03-23
variables:
  analysis_id:
    description: Unique identifier for this analysis record.
    primary_key: true
    type: character
    type_sql: VARCHAR(255)
    validations:
      - col_is_character: []
      - col_vals_not_null:
          label: "analysis_id is required"
      - rows_distinct:
          label: "analysis_id values are unique"
  event_id:
    description: Event (participant × timepoint) this measurement belongs to.
    foreign_key: event.event_id
    type: character
    type_sql: VARCHAR(255)
    validations:
      - col_is_character: []
      - col_vals_not_null:
          label: "event_id is required"
  concentration_ng_ml:
    description: Measured concentration in ng/mL
    type: numeric
    type_sql: DECIMAL
    validations:
      - col_is_numeric: []

How custom codebooks are treated

Once a custom YAML is in place, all beFAIR functions work with it automatically:

  • codebookToSummary() — lists the custom codebook in a separate “Custom codebooks” section, annotated with the project name.
  • draftScript() / codebookToEntries() — accept the custom codebook name just like a built-in one.
  • databasePrepareCodebooks() — creates the corresponding database table and tracks the codebook in table_codebook with codebook_origin set to the project directory name.
  • viewCodebookMap() — renders custom codebook nodes in purple to distinguish them from built-in nodes.

Naming conflicts

If a custom codebook file has the same base name as a built-in codebook (e.g. you place codebooks/study/participant.yaml in your project), beFAIR will stop with an error listing the conflicting name. Always choose names that do not clash with the built-in codebooks.
